note: One controlled case per declared refusal, plus a positive case that must earn none. Each defeating case must earn EXACTLY the code it names: a case that fires for a second reason has not proved the one it is for, and two refusals that cannot be separated are one rule wearing two names. The lines and crosswalk entries are the oracle's own; no case reads STATUS.yaml, so a repair to the live file cannot quietly stop a refusal from being proved.
revision_note: v2 answers an independent observation against commit 5dbe513 (reports/observations/2026-08-27-status-claims-typed-witness-observation.json). The witness got a false standing past v1 by declaring artifact_standing WITNESSED with a non-TOKEN source on a value reading NOT_WITNESSED, and dissolved a collision by renaming a subject. v1's seven cases became twelve, and v1's RULING_TYPED_AS_ACCEPTANCE was widened into a total rule after the witness typed an owner acceptance as a status unrefused.

cases.proves: A field typed with the derived subject, the kind its value's prefix admits, and a token-backed standing earns no refusal.
An entry missing a required field is refused rather than raising. Before this, a missing artifact_standing raised KeyError and a null subject raised TypeError inside sorted().

crosswalk.subject: asset-service
crosswalk.detail: an entry that never declares a standing at all

cases.proves: A status field the crosswalk does not type is a defect, so the typing cannot silently fall behind the document.
A status field the strict reader cannot parse is named rather than skipped. An indented field would otherwise be invisible and earn no FIELD_UNTYPED, letting the reader define its own scope.
A crosswalk entry naming a field and value the document no longer carries is a defect, so the typing cannot outlive what it types.

crosswalk.subject: retired-thing
crosswalk.detail: a claim the document has since dropped

cases.proves: The subject is derived from the field, not declared. A witness dissolved a real collision by renaming one side of it to byom-ruling; a derived subject cannot be renamed.

crosswalk.subject: byom-ruling
crosswalk.detail: a subject renamed to escape a collision

cases.proves: A kind outside the declared three is refused. A witness typo'd RULING as RULLING, which split the collision group and silently disabled the kind rules, because those compare kind strings literally.

crosswalk.subject: ticket-kind-vocabulary
crosswalk.detail: a typo that would disable the rules keyed on this field

cases.proves: Two claims of one kind about one subject stay a duplicate. Typing distinguishes a status from a ruling; it does not excuse writing one subject's status twice. Two identical entries earn this too, which is why a separate duplicate-entry refusal would be the same rule twice.

crosswalk.subject: proofing-service
crosswalk.detail: a second status claim about the same subject

cases.proves: The rule is total in both directions. A witness retyped an accepted packet value as a plain status and v1 admitted it, because v1 guarded only the ruling-and-acceptance pair. OWNER_ACCEPTANCE is irreversible and settled by seat:root; STATUS is neither.

crosswalk.subject: specification
crosswalk.detail: an act of the root seat demoted to a reversible status

cases.proves: Artifact standing stays the four-rung ladder AGENTS.md fixes. A new rung cannot be introduced by typing one.

crosswalk.subject: some-thing
crosswalk.detail: a rung the ladder does not have

cases.proves: The exact bypass an independent witness demonstrated against v1: WITNESSED declared on a value reading NOT_WITNESSED, admitted because a non-TOKEN source was never compared to the value and the value does not begin with a ladder word. Thirty-three of forty-eight live entries begin with a non-ladder word, so the door was open for all of them.

crosswalk.subject: sov-operating-agent
crosswalk.detail: a standing asserted with nothing in the value behind it

cases.proves: The T3 trap fires. NOT_WITNESSED contains the token WITNESSED and asserts the opposite, so typing that value as WITNESSED from a token is refused.

crosswalk.subject: record-service
crosswalk.detail: a standing the value denies rather than asserts

cases.proves: A value beginning with a ladder word must be typed from that token. Declaring otherwise there would let an author call a mechanical claim something unverifiable and escape the token check.
